title: Ria Takes Only What She Needs
moral: Taking only what you need and sharing brings balance and happiness.

scenes.summary: Ria the squirrel loves collecting but takes more than she needs.
scenes.text:
Ria the Squirrel Who Took Too Many Things

In a leafy forest full of tall trees, lived a busy squirrel named Ria.

Ria loved collecting things.

Acorns, shiny stones, colorful leaves—she collected them all!

But there was one problem…

Ria took more than she needed.
scenes.image_prompt: cute squirrel collecting many acorns and items in tree, colorful forest cartoon style

scenes.summary: Ria’s habit of collecting too much creates clutter and confusion.
scenes.text:
Every day, Ria gathered acorns.

One… two… ten… twenty!

“Just in case,” she said.

Soon, her tree was filled with piles of stuff.

There was hardly any space left!

Ria tried to find her favorite acorn.

But it was buried under many others.

“Where is it?” she wondered.

She searched and searched.

But couldn’t find it.
scenes.image_prompt: messy tree filled with acorns and squirrel searching confused, cartoon scene

scenes.summary: A strong wind causes Ria to lose control of her belongings.
scenes.text:
One day, a strong wind blew.

Whoooosh!

Some of Ria’s acorns fell out of the tree.

“Oh no!” Ria cried.

“They’re falling everywhere!”
scenes.image_prompt: wind blowing acorns out of tree while squirrel looks worried, lively cartoon

scenes.summary: Pico helps Ria realize she doesn’t need so many things.
scenes.text:
Just then, Pico the Sparrow flew by.

“Why do you have so many?” Pico asked.

“I wanted to keep everything,” Ria said.

Pico smiled.

“Maybe you only need a few,” he said.
scenes.image_prompt: sparrow talking to squirrel about clutter in tree, friendly cartoon style

scenes.summary: Ria organizes her things and shares extras, making her life easier.
scenes.text:
Ria thought for a moment.

She sorted her acorns.

She kept what she needed.

And shared the rest with her friends.

Now her tree was neat and clean.

She could find everything easily.

“This feels so nice!” Ria said.

Take only what you need.

Sharing and organizing make life better.

The End

story:
Ria the Squirrel Who Took Too Many Things

In a leafy forest full of tall trees, lived a busy squirrel named Ria.

Ria loved collecting things.

Acorns, shiny stones, colorful leaves—she collected them all!

But there was one problem…

Ria took more than she needed.

Every day, Ria gathered acorns.

One… two… ten… twenty!

“Just in case,” she said.

Soon, her tree was filled with piles of stuff.

There was hardly any space left!

Ria tried to find her favorite acorn.

But it was buried under many others.

“Where is it?” she wondered.

She searched and searched.

But couldn’t find it.

One day, a strong wind blew.

Whoooosh!

Some of Ria’s acorns fell out of the tree.

“Oh no!” Ria cried.

“They’re falling everywhere!”

Just then, Pico the Sparrow flew by.

“Why do you have so many?” Pico asked.

“I wanted to keep everything,” Ria said.

Pico smiled.

“Maybe you only need a few,” he said.

Ria thought for a moment.

She sorted her acorns.

She kept what she needed.

And shared the rest with her friends.

Now her tree was neat and clean.

She could find everything easily.

“This feels so nice!” Ria said.

Take only what you need.

Sharing and organizing make life better.

The End
